business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: British Columbia, Canada (federal state; provincial corporate law jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Federal and provincial statute law overlaid on English-based common law; British Columbia applies common law doctrine with codified corporate governance under the Business Corporations Act
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force July 1, 2020
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally applied since September 21, 2017
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada since December 30, 2018
Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force October 1, 2014
Convention between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980, as amended by the 5th Protocol, in force 2008)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended, including FINTRAC AML/CFT regulations (SOR/2002-184); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2 (laundering proceeds of crime). Provincial (BC): Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, s. 121.2 (Significant Individuals Transparency Register) and s. 50 (registered office); Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 400/2002, ss. 22-26; Money Laundering Suppression Act, S.B.C. 2020, c. 17, as amended. The transparency register is an internal corporate record; it is not publicly searchable, and access is reserved for FINTRAC, the RCMP, the Canada Revenue Agency, provincial enforcement agencies and regulators on lawful demand. A public beneficial ownership register for BC corporations is under phased implementation by the Provincial Government.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport or national identity document of each proposed director, officer, and beneficial owner holding 25% or more of shares or control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Commissioner for Taking Affidavits in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the document's country of origin (Canada acceded to the HCCH 1961 Apostille Convention, effective January 11, 2024); for non-Hague states, consular legalization via Global Affairs Canada and the relevant embassy or consulate remains mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance for any existing parent or shareholder entity, including parent-level UBO breakdown
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Director under s. 217 of the BCBCA (BC Corporate Registry) or the analogous foreign corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for use in Canada; consular legalization only for instruments originating in non-Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration from each subscriber to the incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed issuing bank or Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille when issued abroad; where the declaration is sworn in BC before a commissioner for oaths or notary, no apostille is required domestically

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to Act as Director (statutory form filed with the Notice of Articles under s. 124 BCBCA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BC Corporate Registry via BC Corporate Online
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Digitally filed federal/provincial form; no notarization or apostille required for filing, but a notarized counterpart may be required by corporate account banks and Steam/PlayStation payment onboarding

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Significant Individuals Transparency Register record (company-side statutory register of individuals with significant control)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporation agent / legal counsel maintaining the registered record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal statutory record; disclosed to FINTRAC, RCMP, CRA and provincial regulators upon lawful request; retained for a minimum of 7 years after termination of the business relationship

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, significant shareholders, and Steam/PlayStation payout counterparties against: (i) FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) definitions, covering domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates under the PCMLTFA Regulations; (ii) the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; and (iv) Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists maintained under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. Screening must occur pre-incorporation, at annual review, and upon any material ownership or control change, with results and risk assessments documented and retained for a minimum of 5 years. For this Low_Risk_Standard gaming-publishing profile, standard due diligence applies; however, any positive PEP match or source-of-funds anomaly automatically escalates the file to enhanced due diligence requiring independent legal certification and, if warranted, a suspicious transaction report to FINTRAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca) and the OneStop Business Registry (onestop.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Roman letters, Arabic numerals and permitted punctuation; English-only is the standard for BC provincial incorporation, and there is no French-language requirement at the provincial level. Accents are permitted; non-Roman scripts (e.g., CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic) must be transliterated into English before submission. A NUANS-style name search is embedded in the mandatory BC Name Request process. A distinctive element must be combined with a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or 'Company', and commonly used corporate suffixes may not be abbreviated inconsistently with the BCBCA.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC Name Request is reserved for 56 days. An extension request (CORP NRX filing through BC Corporate Online) must be submitted to the Corporate Registry before expiration and is granted at the Registrar's discretion. Upon name rejection, the incorporator may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the refusal, citing s. 26 of the BCBCA and ss. 22-26 of the Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 400/2002. If reconsideration is refused, judicial review may be commenced in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, generally within 60 days of the final decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with strict compliance: s. 50 of the BCBCA requires a physical street address in British Columbia at which process can be served; P.O. Box addresses are prohibited. The registered office must be open for business purposes for a minimum of 6 hours per business day. For ISIC 5820 digital publishing, licensing a registered-office address and virtual mail-scan service from a licensed BC corporate services provider is legally acceptable. However, Steam (Valve Corporation) and PlayStation Store (Sony Interactive Entertainment) payout account KYC procedures require disclosure of a physical principal place of business, which may be the directors' office or a home office if reasonably maintained. A purely virtual office without any physical BC presence should be disclosed to each payment platform to avoid onboarding delays or payout holds.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 5% cumulative probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 36 months for a Low_Risk_Standard digital-game publisher; no statutory inspection regime is specific to ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210. The Corporate Registry may verify registered-office validity upon third-party complaint, and the CRA or FINTRAC may conduct a compliance visit only upon material risk indicators. Probability would materially increase (above 30%) if the entity were registered as a money-services business, which is outside the current scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57; Part 2 (Incorporation), ss. 9-15; Registered and Records Offices, s. 16; Officers, s. 128
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Incorporation Agreement (Form 2) filed electronically via Corporate Online; Certificate of Incorporation is issued upon registration (online fee CA$350)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the Business Corporations Act; one or more shares without par value may be issued for nominal consideration. No statutory escrow account requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that this Corporation accept the subscription of common voting shares without par value by the founding shareholder and that such shares be issued fully paid and non-assessable upon receipt of lawful consideration. RESOLVED, that the registered office and corporate records office of this Corporation be established at the address shown on the Notice of Articles, British Columbia, and be maintained with the corporate seal and minute book. RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: President, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary to hold office until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED, that banking accounts be opened at the Corporation's chartered bank with two-signature authority and that all instruments necessary to implement these resolutions be executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and NUANS Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online), Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access Corporate Online, authenticate, and file a Name Reservation Request with up to three proposed corporate names in the standard 'C' format; attach the NUANS search report; pay the reservation fee online; obtain the Name Reservation Certificate valid for 56 days. Electronic submission requires no notarization.
required_dossiers: List of up to three proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on distinctiveness or confusion grounds, file a fresh Name Reservation Request with a more distinctive element, or apply for a registry review of the refusal before the 56-day reservation period expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing via Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Notice of Articles) and Form 2 (Incorporation Agreement) online; elect one class of no-par common voting shares; appoint one or more directors (no Canadian residency requirement under BC law); provide physical registered office and records office addresses in BC; file director consents to act; submit electronically and pay the CA$350 registration fee to receive the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director for each director
Registered office and records office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Registry requisition within 30 days by correcting the electronic filing; if the certificate has issued with an error, apply for administrative correction through the Corporate Online correction workflow.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and Tax Account Registration (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for a 9-digit Federal Business Number (BN) and the program accounts applicable to digital publishing: corporate income tax (RC0001) and GST/HST (RC0001) accounts; add a payroll account (RP0001) once employees are engaged. Confirm eligibility for Canadian-controlled private corporation status. No notarization is required for the BRO flow.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA issues a data-match query, respond through Represent a Client within 30 days with corrected entity information; escalate unresolved issues via the CRA Business Window at 1-800-959-5525.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Ministry of Finance (eTax BC) and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a BC PST account through eTax BC if taxable digital products are supplied to BC consumers; register the employer with WorkSafeBC under the Workers Compensation Act for office personnel and obtain a clearance letter; account separately for Steam and PlayStation payout revenue versus direct BC consumer sales.
required_dossiers: Revenue model description for digital store payouts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If PST registration is held for review, file a written clarification of the digital goods supply chain; for WorkSafeBC, correct industry classification codes through the WorkSafeBC account portal before the coverage effective date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal General Business Licence and Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver, Licence and Permits (or applicable BC municipality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a General Business Licence for the registered premises using the municipal e-licensing system; submit the lease, floor plan, and zoning confirmation; schedule the BC Fire Code inspection and arrange for the licence certificate to be displayed at the premises. No separate provincial industry permit is mandated for ISIC 5820 digital publishing.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused for zoning nonconformity, apply to the municipal board of variance for a minor variance, or relocate to a conforming commercial zone and re-file the licence application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online) and the Company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass written board consents in lieu of meeting; adopt the Model By-laws (Form 3) unless customized articles are filed; execute the first board resolution covering share issuance, registered office, and officer appointments; prepare the minute book, securities register, and registers of directors and members; file the first annual report within two months after the anniversary of incorporation.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual report is filed late, pay the reinstatement fee and file through Corporate Online under the registry's compliance reinstatement process; correct any officer or registered-office inaccuracies by filing the applicable change notice through Corporate Online.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial or federal industry licence is mandated for ISIC 5820 digital publishing; municipal licensing authority: City of Vancouver Licence and Permits; workplace authority: WorkSafeBC
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Licence issued under the Vancouver Charter, S.B.C. 1953, c. 55, s. 289; no sector-specific operating permit is required for PC and console digital game publishing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy and Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt: no reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 43; an office-only digital publisher falls outside all reviewable project classes
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharges; office wastewater conveyed to municipal sewer under B.C. Reg. 87/2012; electronic waste (servers and test consoles) managed under B.C. Reg. 103/2004; GHG reporting threshold of 10,000 tCO2e not applicable at this footprint

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code (Division B, Part 2) issued by municipal fire prevention; structural load inspection for server racks and equipment per BC Building Code 2018, Part 4; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance under the Workers Compensation Act, including emergency planning and ergonomic workstation assessment

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), federal tax administration portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; British Columbia Ministry of Finance (Provincial Sales Tax) portal: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first incorporate as a Business Corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the British Columbia Business Corporations Act; then apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) via the 'Register for a business number' online service or Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Program Accounts). The entity must open corporate income tax (RC2) and Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) program accounts; a payroll (RP) account is required if Canadian employees are hired. Thereafter, the corporation must register for British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) through eTaxBC before making taxable sales of goods or software in BC, and enrol for BC Employer Health Tax if remuneration exceeds CAD 500,000. A non-resident corporation with Canadian-source income must obtain a BN to file Part I corporate returns and may be subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on cross-border payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Canadian-resident corporation is taxed in its own right under Part I of the Income Tax Act on worldwide income, with no pass-through treatment; a non-resident corporation is taxable on Canadian-source employment, business, and capital gains income, and on Canadian-source investment income subject to Part XIII withholding; BC has no separate corporate income tax and applies the federal provincial tax allocation system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists. Available statutory elections include: section 216 election for anon-resident to compute tax on Canadian rental/timber income on a net basis; section 217 election for non-residents to pay Canadian tax on registered retirement savings plan income; section 39(2) functional currency election to report Canadian tax results in Canadian dollars; section 18(4)/18.5 hybrid-mismatch limitation rules to deny double deduction; GST/HST elections such as section 156 associated-persons election and the quick-method election for small suppliers under the Excise Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) is a destination-based value-added tax; British Columbia levied rate is 5% GST only (BC does not participate in the HST). BC also imposes a separate non-creditable Provincial Sales Tax (PST) at 7% on retail sales of taxable goods and specified software, plus incremental PST surtaxes (e.g., 0.5% TransLink vehicle tax) and the BC Employer Health Tax; digital game supply via Steam/PlayStation to BC consumers attracts 5% GST and, where applicable, 7% PST on deemed downloaded software.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold); the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies to non-resident digital-services suppliers making taxable supplies to Canadian consumers; BC PST registration is required for any person making taxable sales in BC, without a general small-supplier exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory government e-invoicing clearance regime. GST/HST registrants with annual taxable revenue above CAD 1.5 million must file returns electronically (GST/HST NETFILE, EDI, or CRA My Business Account); all invoices must be retained as original business records. The CRA promotes voluntary PEPPOL BIS 3.0 e-invoicing interoperability for procurement but does not mandate any specific API or pre-clearance validation. Registered non-resident digital-services suppliers file simplified quarterly GST/HST returns electronically through My Business Account.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act applies: (a) goods physically exported by the supplier and delivered to a destination outside Canada (sections 1-2); (b) services supplied to a non-resident provided the service is performed wholly outside Canada, or if performed in Canada the foreign recipient does not consume or use the service in Canada and no supply relates to Canadian real property or tangible personal property in Canada (section 7); (c) intangible personal property, including digital game licences, software rights, and Steam/PlayStation publishing rights, supplied to a non-resident for use exclusively outside Canada and not exploited in Canada (section 10). For a BC corporate publisher, sales of digital keys or publishing services to Valve/Steam or PlayStation Store operators for international customers are zero-rated if the contract, jurisdiction-of-use clauses, and non-resident status of the licensee support use outside Canada; domestic Canadian end-user downloads remain taxable. Canada does not impose a statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is used operationally as a CRA documentation-acceptance reference, and evidence of export and receipt within a reasonable commercial period is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CRA Export Declaration (Form B13A) or Canada Border Services Agency Automated Export System (CAED/ATLAS) filing for physical goods
Commercial Invoice and Publishing / Distribution Licence Agreement with Valve (Steam) or PlayStation Store operator
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or electronic delivery log evidencing movement of exported goods outside Canada
Carrier, customs broker, or freight-forwarder proof of export certificate (date-stamped)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103, bank statement, or payment processor payout evidence showing foreign-currency receipt and conversion
Certificate of Residence of the foreign licensee or Form W-8BEN-E demonstrating non-resident status for Canadian tax purposes
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess GST/HST net tax within the normal four-year limitation period under section 298 of the Excise Tax Act; the limitation extends to ten years where a taxpayer has been negligent or careless, and is unlimited in cases of fraud or willful misrepresentation. Specific penalties include: section 280 failure to register or collect GST/HST equals 15% of unreported tax; section 280(1.1) late filing penalty of 5% of unassessed net tax; section 285 gross-negligence penalty of 50% of any misstatement or omission; section 286 penalty for false refund claims equal to 50% of the overstated refund plus arrears interest. Zero-rated export claims are screened under the CRA Export Verification and Zero-Rated Supplies audit programs; where documentary substantiation fails, the CRA disallows the zero-rating, claws back refunds and input tax credits retroactively, adds interest from the date the refund was originally paid, and may refer fraudulent export filings for criminal prosecution under section 327.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); FX-related statutory administration co-led by FINTRAC (PCMLTFA enforcement), Global Affairs Canada (sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act), and OSFI (prudential supervision of authorized banks)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current- and capital-account convertibility with a freely floating Canadian dollar (no general exchange-control permit regime since repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1952). Profit remittance is unrestricted at the FX level; practical hurdles are limited to: Part XIII withholding tax on dividends (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced typically to 5%–15%), CRA non-resident payment reporting and slip filing requirements, regulatory approval only for payments touching sanctioned persons/regimes, and currency-reporting thresholds for cross-border movements of monetary instruments exceeding C$10,000.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement, mandatory conversion ratio, or prescribed repatriation timeline applies to Canadian export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in any currency and in any authorized account. Only reporting obligations apply: FINTRAC cross-border currency and monetary instrument reports (C$10,000+), financial-entity large-value transaction reports (C$10,000+), and sanctions-screening obligations; no central bank declaration is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational CAD Account + US$ Foreign Currency Account (dual-ledger structure)
Operational CAD Account + US$ Settlement Account
Operational CAD Account + Global Banking & Markets USD Facility
Operational CAD Account + Cross-Border Banking USD Rail
Operational CAD Account + US$ Clearing Account
Operational CAD Account (US$ clearing via correspondent)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — FINTRAC-registered Money Service Businesses (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Stripe, Airwallex) are viable for USD payouts from Steam/Valve and PlayStation and for low-cost FX conversion, but they do not hold a Payments Canada Lynx/ACSS clearing license, cannot issue CAD routing documents for bank-verification purposes with Valve, and may not be used as the sole settlement bank under Part XIII/compliance treasury policy; an integrated Schedule I bank deposit account remains the mandatory anchor rail. EEA-style Electronic-Money-Institution authorizations have no legal standing in Canada and do not substitute for MSB registration or banking license requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid with de facto in-person mandate — for a private BC Business Corporation with non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners, Canadian Schedule I banks uniformly require at least one in-branch interview (Vancouver or Toronto) with a director/officer authorized at the 25% signing threshold; FINTRAC-compliant verification requires government-issued photo ID plus a second identity document. Remote video-based client identification is permitted under revised PCMLTFA guidelines since May 2021, but is offered only discretionarily for low-risk digital-publishing entities with full corporate documentation; physical presence is the established norm for year-one onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% foreign ownership / non-resident beneficial-owner concentration, creating a classic shell-company red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Registry Statement of Information and company search; BC Transparency Register extract; group organogram to ultimate beneficial owner; notarized passports; PEP declarations; source-of-wealth letter; audited parent financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High expected turnover from Steam/PlayStation digital payouts with no traditional invoices or physical trade documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valve Steamworks Publishing Agreement; PlayStation Partner/Publisher Agreement; last six months of platform net-revenue payout statements; game catalogue and title registrations; revenue-recognition accounting policy; CRA Notice of Assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Parent or UBO linked to a high-risk jurisdiction or appearing on sanctions/raised-monitoring lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions screening result; World-Check/LexisNexis diligence report from the bank; internal sanctions screening policy; external legal opinion under Special Economic Measures Act; OFAC-non-blocking confirmation if US exposure exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sources of injected capital originating from crypto exchanges or unexplained third-party accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chain-of-funds trace of the MT103 equity-injection wire; foreign shareholder bank statements; shareholder resolution approving capital contribution; no-crypto attestation; exchange withdrawal confirmation with transaction logs if derived from virtual-asset liquidation; CRA crypto-asset filing position.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived lack of physical substance (registered-office-only address)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC lease or sublease agreement; payroll/T4 summary demonstrating BC employees; registered-office services agreement; operational report detailing live game publishing workflow; BC business-address confirmation; utility bill matching corporate records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder equity must route as a SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pain.001 via API banking) from the foreign parent to the BC Corporation's CAD operational account with explicit purpose code 'Direct Investment–Equity Injection' and narrative 'Paid-up share capital contribution'; the entry is recorded as increased paid-in capital on the corporate ledger. For intercompany loans, compliance requires thin-capitalization adherence (debt-to-equity not exceeding 1.5:1 effective 2024) and documented term-sheet covenants. Any receipt exceeding C$10,000 triggers the bank's FINTRAC large-value transaction report; the bank performs sanctions screening on the remitter before crediting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Steam/Valve and PlayStation Store settlement flows are inbound: USD credited via US ACH direct deposit or SWIFT MT103 into the entity's US$ ledger account, then converted to CAD via the bank's FX desk. Outbound operational disbursements (royalties to IP owners, engine license fees, overseas studio COGS, and dividends to the foreign parent) use: SWIFT MT103 wires for values over C$50,000; US FedACH/SWIFT for USD-denominated payments; Payments Canada Lynx for high-value same-day CAD settlement; ACSS for domestic batched CAD payments; and SEPA/SEPA Instant for euro-denominated counterparties. Commercial letters of credit are not market-standard for downloadable-game licensing and are therefore not used; settlement relies on contractual net-30/net-60 terms evidenced by platform payout statements and escrow-cleared milestone confirmations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable plain-vanilla FX forward contracts (USD/CAD; EUR/CAD) up to 12-month tenor
FX swap/rollover contracts to extend hedging tenors
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) for matched long-term intercompany liabilities
OTC vanilla FX options (call/put) executed under ISDA/CSA margin documentation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for restricted offshore settlement currencies (e.g., KRW, TWD, PHP) only where platform-generated residual exposure exists; permitted for hedging purposes only under OSFI derivative guidelines and internal treasury policy, with speculative trading contractually prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report and Transparency Register Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registry, BC Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 calendar months after the corporation's incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: On-time fee CAD 40; late filing total CAD 106.20; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes the registrar to administratively strike off the company; restoration requires registrar consent or court order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return including BC provincial corporate tax schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance-due day is 2 months after year-end (3 months for CCPCs claiming the small business deduction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat non-filers pay 10% plus 2% per month; daily compounded arrears interest; wilful failure may trigger prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and annual resolutions record (internal corporate record, no registry filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the BC registered office; no external filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter at least once each calendar year and no more than 15 months after the previous AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary penalty; directors may be exposed to breach of fiduciary duty proceedings; omission impairs subsequent amalgamation, continuation, or dissolution filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based mandatory audit for private BC business corporations; audit requirement waived by unanimous shareholder resolution under BC BCA; audit becomes mandatory if shareholders holding at least 5% of issued voting shares requisition an auditor appointment or the waiver is revoked.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private enterprises, used for T2 corporate income tax reporting and financial schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under BC BCA Part 11.1 the company must maintain a Transparency Register of significant individuals (25% or more share interest, control, or de facto control); the register must be updated within 14 days of any share transfer or change in significant control; an annual transparency report is filed with the BC Annual Report confirming the register is current; non-compliance is an offence carrying fines up to CAD 50,000 for the corporation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 75-260 per year for BC registered office and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-18,000 for a full certified audit; commonly waived by unanimous shareholder resolution in a private BC single-owner publisher, with a review engagement (USD 2,000-5,000) or notice-to-reader engagement prepared instead

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED tax credit (refundable up to 35% for CCPCs), BC Digital Media Tax Credit (17.5% refundable for eligible activities), federal Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (15% refundable for qualifying corporations)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed via CRA My Business Account or approved tax software (e.g., TurboTax, Taxprep)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., for December 31 year-end, deadline is June 30)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (line 300) - net income after adjustments, including non-resident income attributable to Canadian business
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must report Canadian-source business income and may claim treaty relief if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax (line 310) - calculated at 15% general rate or 9% for CCPC on first CAD 500,000 active business income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are subject to federal tax on Canadian business income; treaty rates may apply

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax (line 400) - BC provincial tax at 12% general rate or 2% for CCPC on first CAD 500,000 active business income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are subject to BC provincial tax on income earned in BC; no separate provincial return required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable (line 500) - sum of federal and provincial tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Total tax payable includes both federal and provincial components

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax (line 580) - Part XIII tax on dividends, royalties, interest paid to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report and remit withholding tax on payments to non-residents; treaty rates may reduce the amount

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (line 600) - SR&ED, DMC, IDMTC, and other refundable/non-refundable credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim credits only if they have Canadian-source income and are subject to Canadian tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net balance due (line 700) - tax payable minus credits and installments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due must be paid by the filing deadline; interest applies on late payments

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months (10% plus 2% per month if repeat offender). Interest on unpaid taxes at prescribed rate (currently 9% for corporations).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (reduced by tax treaties, e.g., 15% under Canada-US treaty for portfolio dividends, 5% for substantial shareholding)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, non-resident recipient must provide Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty) and a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from their tax authority. Payer must withhold at treaty rate if form is valid before payment; otherwise statutory rate applies and recipient may claim refund via Canadian tax return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, treaty rate often 10% (e.g., Canada-US treaty) or 0% for certain copyright royalties. Interest: statutory 25%, treaty rate often 10% (arm's length) or 0% for certain types.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 10 million gross revenue and CAD 1 million cross-border transactions with non-residents (per CRA guidelines)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a specific ESR, but CRA applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) to deny tax benefits from transactions lacking economic substance. Treaty benefits may be denied under Limitation on Benefits (LOB) provisions if entity lacks substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully evading or attempting to evade tax by false statements, omission of income, or fraudulent claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 200% of tax evaded, plus interest. Criminal prosecution: fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for corporate tax debts if they participated in evasion; may face civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a shell corporation with no economic substance to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions or avoid Canadian tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reassess and apply GAAR, adding tax, interest, and penalties up to 50% of tax avoided. Treaty benefits may be denied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for tax if they knowingly participated; may face civil penalties and potential criminal charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register with FINTRAC, failure to report large cash transactions or suspicious transactions, or failure to maintain compliance program
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for first offense; criminal charges up to CAD 2 million and imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for penalties if they knowingly or negligently failed to comply; may face travel bans and imprisonment.
